info.title: SoulCloud API
info.description: Device management for MQTT 5 devices. Human users authenticate with a bearer session token (POST /v1/auth/login). Device-facing endpoints are under /v1/device/.

token.description: Shown once. Hand it to the device during provisioning.

deviceId.description: The device created when the token was redeemed

password.description: Shown once; store it in NVS

hardwareId.description: Stable hardware identity, e.g. the base MAC address

id.description: Also the MQTT username and client id

health.description: Heap, RSSI and device-defined extras from the last heartbeat

id.description: Sent to the device as MQTT 5 correlation data

code.description: Exit code reported by the device

nextBefore.description: Pass as `before` for the next (older) page

loggedAt.description: Estimated wall-clock time (binary logs with a time sync)

decoded.description: False for binary entries that could not be rendered (e.g. no ELF)

raw.description: Base64 packet bytes of binary entries that were not decoded

hasElf.description: Whether binary logs from this firmware can be decoded

post.summary: Create an account. The first account becomes an admin.
Sign in with email and password
Create a single-use pairing token for a new device
Redeem a pairing token (called by the device)
post.description: Returns fresh MQTT credentials. Every enrollment yields a new device id and password.

delete.description: Its credentials stop working immediately and its connection is closed. History is kept.

get.summary: Recent heartbeats (uptime and health history), newest first

get.description: Other method names are sent to the device as-is with free-form params.

post.summary: Send a request to a device (MQTT 5 request/response)
post.description: The command is delivered when the device is (or next comes) online, until it expires. With `wait`, the call returns as soon as the device answers or the wait elapses.

schema.description: Seconds to wait for the device's response before returning

parameters.description: Seconds to wait for the device's response before returning
parameters.name: wait

schema.description: Return commands older than this command id

parameters.description: Return commands older than this command id
parameters.name: before

post.summary: Run a debug shell line and wait for its output

200.description: Result (output is null if the device didn't answer in time)

get.summary: One command; with `wait`, long-poll until it completes

schema.description: Seconds to wait for the device's response before returning

parameters.description: Seconds to wait for the device's response before returning
parameters.name: wait

get.summary: Device logs, newest first (or oldest first with `after`)
get.description: Binary (on9log) entries are decoded with the ELF uploaded for the firmware the device was running.

get.summary: Raw on9log stream for offline decoding
get.description: Binary log packets as typed SLIP frames, the format the on9log host CLI replays: `on9log --log-bin <file> --elf <firmware.elf>`.

post.summary: Upload a firmware image (and optionally its ELF)
post.description: Version, chip and ELF hash are read from the image itself. The ELF is needed to decode binary (on9log) logs and must be the one the image was built from.

delete.summary: Delete firmware that no OTA job uses

put.summary: Attach the ELF to an uploaded firmware
put.description: Binary logs already received from this firmware become decodable.

get.summary: Download a firmware image (signed URL from ota.start)

post.description: Online devices start right away; offline ones start when they next connect or ask (ota.check).

get.summary: One OTA job with per-device progress

post.description: Devices already verifying or rebooting into the new image are left to finish.

get.summary: A device's OTA history, newest first
